connectDrawer.title: Connect to this database
connectDrawer.description: Connection strings for this engine. Copy one into your app or client.
connectDrawer.passwordNote: Passwords are never shown here. Replace <password> with a credential from the Access page.
connectDrawer.tunnelTitle: No public port? Use a tunnel
connectDrawer.tunnelBody: The CLI opens a local port that relays to this database through the control plane. Nothing is exposed to the internet.
connectDrawer.tunnelAfter: The command prints a connection string for the local port. Add --launch to start psql, mysql or redis-cli automatically (set LEVELRAIL_DB_PASSWORD first).

external.badgeHint: Levelrail connects to this database but does not run it.

connect.title: Connect an existing database
connect.description: Point apps at a database where it already runs. Nothing is moved, copied or changed on the database itself.
connect.sourceAdoptHint: Pick a running database container. It is only read, never stopped, restarted or modified.
connect.sourceManualHint: A database on another host, a managed service, or anything you can reach by address.
connect.toast: Connected "{{name}}". Nothing was changed on the database.
connect.adoptSafe: Adopting does not stop, restart, recreate or modify this container, and does not attach it to any network.
connect.noCandidates: No running database containers were found on this server. Enter the connection details instead.
connect.candidatesError: Could not list containers on this node.

fields.name: Name
fields.nameHint: Apps reference this name, for example {{example}}.
fields.hostHint: A hostname, an IP address, or a container name on the network below. Not localhost.
fields.networkHint: Optional. The network the database container is attached to, so Levelrail and your apps can reach it by name.
fields.passwordHint: Stored encrypted. It is never shown again unless an admin reveals it.

next.slow: The database answered, but slowly. Check load on the database host and the network between the two.
next.auth_failed: The database refused the user or password. Check them, and that this host is allowed to connect (for Postgres, pg_hba.conf).
next.tls_error: TLS did not match what the server expects. Switch the TLS setting between Off, If available and Required.
next.unreachable: Nothing answered at this address. Check the host, port and Docker network, and that the database is running.
next.unknown: The check could not run. See the detail, then try again.

overview.title: Connection
overview.description: Levelrail connects to this database where it runs. It does not manage its container, volume or version.
overview.revealNote: Revealing is recorded in the audit log.
overview.usedBy: Use it from an app: set an env var to {{ref}}.

delete.title: Remove "{{name}}" from Levelrail?
delete.description: This only removes Levelrail's record and its stored password. The database, its container and all of its data are not touched. Apps that use it lose their connection settings.
delete.toast: Removed "{{name}}". The database itself was not touched.

delete.title: Delete "{{name}}"?
delete.description: This stops the database and removes it from Levelrail. Its data volume and backups in your storage destination are kept, so the data can still be recovered by an operator. Apps that connect to it will lose the connection.
delete.inUseDescription: Delete anyway only if you have already moved or detached these apps.
delete.typedHint: Apps connected to it lose the connection.

version.title: Change version of "{{name}}"
version.description: Minor and patch updates recreate the container over the same data. A major version change needs the guarded major upgrade (Postgres) below, or a backup restored into a new database. Take a backup first.
version.label: Version
version.toast: Database "{{name}}" will be recreated on version {{version}}.
version.pgvectorHint: A pgvector database uses a version like "17-pgvector". Switching between plain and pgvector in place is refused: use the guarded major upgrade below, or restore a backup into a new database.

existingVolume.title: A deleted database with this name left its data behind
existingVolume.description: Choose what to do with the old data volume ({{size}}). Reusing it brings the old data back; discarding it deletes it permanently and starts empty.

walShip.label: WAL copy in bucket
walShip.hint: Archived WAL is copied to the backup target so point-in-time restore survives losing this host's disk.

pitrNew.enableBinlog: Enable continuous binary log archiving so this database can be restored to any exact moment, not just to when a backup happened to run.
pitrNew.title: Restore {{name}} to a point in time
pitrNew.description: This creates a new database from a base backup plus the archived binary log up to the chosen time. {{name}} is not changed.
pitrNew.replayFrom: Replaying from the base backup taken {{when}}.
pitrNew.noBackup: No succeeded base backup exists at or before that time.
pitrNew.newNameHint: A new {{engine}} database with this name is created.
pitrNew.startedBody: The new database appears in the list once it is created. This table updates when it finishes.

majorUpgrade.title: Major version upgrade
majorUpgrade.description: Upgrades this database across a major version by dump and restore. It is offline while it runs. The old data is copied to a rollback snapshot first, and a failure after that rolls back automatically.
majorUpgrade.confirmLabel: Type the database name to confirm
majorUpgrade.rollbackConfirm: Roll back to version {{version}}? Every write since the upgrade is lost.
majorUpgrade.discardConfirm: Delete the rollback snapshot? You can no longer roll back this upgrade.
majorUpgrade.pitrBlocked: Disable point-in-time restore before upgrading: its base backups cannot be replayed on another major version.
majorUpgrade.pgvectorHint: Use a version like "17-pgvector" to move a plain database onto the pgvector image. Moving back to plain Postgres is not supported.

viewer.unsupported: The viewer supports Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, and Redis-compatible engines. This database is {{engine}}.
viewer.notRunning: The viewer needs a running database. Start the database and try again.

beta.label: Beta
beta.hint: Beta: not tuned for large databases or heavy load yet. We improve it every release.

explorer.title: Explorer
explorer.empty: No user tables yet. Create a table and it will show up here.
explorer.selectTable: Select a table to browse its data, columns, and indexes.
explorer.truncated: Showing the first {{count}} tables only. Narrow the search or raise the server limit.

data.filterHint: Type in a column filter row to narrow rows in the database. Prefix with = for an exact match, or use is:null and not:null.
data.limitsNote: Rows load {{page}} at a time. The server returns at most {{rows}} rows per request, cuts any value at {{cell}}, and stops a query after {{seconds}} seconds.

grid.resultCapped: Result capped by the server row or size limit.
grid.cellCapped: This value was cut at the server cell size limit.
grid.label: Table rows
grid.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard.
grid.headerHint: Click to sort. Drag to reorder, or press Alt with the arrow keys.

console.title: SQL Console
console.explainHint: Explain analyze executes the statement (read-only) to report real timings.
console.shortcut: Run with Ctrl or Cmd plus Enter
console.writeToggleHint: Admin only. Runs one statement in a committed transaction and is recorded in the audit log.
console.writeConfirmDescription: Statements run in this console will change data in "{{name}}" and are committed immediately. Each one is recorded in the audit log. Type the database name to continue.
console.noResultsYet: Run a statement to see results here.
console.okNoRows: Statement ran. It returned no rows.

history.empty: Your recent statements for this database show up here.

saved.empty: Save a statement to reuse it later.

keys.title: Key browser
keys.selectKey: Select a key to see its value.
keys.truncated: Value cut at the server limit.
keys.readOnlyNote: Read-only. Values are fetched with SCAN, TYPE, TTL, and a type-specific read.

structure.noRelations: This table has no foreign keys and nothing references it.

states.loading: Reading the schema from the database...
states.errorNote: This does not mean your data is gone. The explorer could not read it right now.

reason.permission: The database refused the read: permission denied for the account the explorer uses.
reason.connection: The database is not accepting connections yet, or refused this one.
reason.timeout: The database took too long to answer and the read timed out.
reason.notRunning: The database is not running. Start it and retry.
reason.helper: The helper that runs inside the database container failed before it could return a schema.
reason.network: The browser could not reach the control plane.
reason.unsupported: This control plane cannot run commands inside database containers.

states.emptyVerifyTitle: No tables found, check this against the evidence below
states.emptyBody: This database was checked and has no user tables. Create tables from the SQL console, or point an app at it.
states.migrationTarget: This database was created as a migration target.
states.copyCli: or run: migrate db-copy <database> with the CLI.
states.verifiedEmpty: The copy is marked verified but the database has no tables. A verified copy should never be empty, so treat this as an error and run the copy again.
states.contradiction_one: The catalog reports {{count}} table but the listing returned none. Retry, and if this persists check the helper logs.
states.contradiction_other: The catalog reports {{count}} tables but the listing returned none. Retry, and if this persists check the helper logs.

evidence.tables: Tables and views in those schemas
evidence.unavailable: The catalog counts could not be read, so this emptiness is not verified.

states.noMatchesNote: The database has tables. Only your search filtered them out.

engineStats.title: No data browser for {{engine}}
engineStats.description: There is no table or key browser for {{engine}}: read and write it through its HTTP API from a connected app. Live counts from the engine are below.
engineStats.descriptionCache: Memcached cannot list its keys, so there is nothing to browse. Live server stats are below.
engineStats.emptyObjects: No indexes or collections yet. They appear here once an app creates one.
engineStats.errorBody: The engine did not answer. Check that the database is running, then try again.

createFlavor.label: Postgres image
createFlavor.hint: Runs {{image}} so its extensions are available with CREATE EXTENSION. The version is stored as {{version}}. Changing flavor later is a guarded dump and restore, not an in-place switch.
createFlavor.hintNone: The official Postgres image, no extra extensions.

picker.databaseDescription: Pick an engine. Credentials, networking and backups are set up for you.
picker.searchPlaceholder: Search engines, for example Postgres or Redis
picker.genericTagline: A managed {{label}} database, ready to use.

taglines.postgres: The default choice for apps that need joins, transactions and constraints.
taglines.pgvector: Postgres with vector similarity search for embeddings and RAG.
taglines.timescaledb: Postgres tuned for metrics, events and other time series.
taglines.postgis: Postgres with geospatial types, indexes and queries.
taglines.mysql: The widely hosted relational engine behind most PHP and CMS stacks.
taglines.mariadb: Community-driven MySQL fork with a familiar protocol and tooling.
taglines.redis: In-memory store for caches, queues, sessions and rate limits.
taglines.valkey: Open source Redis fork under the Linux Foundation, drop-in for Redis clients.
taglines.keydb: Multithreaded Redis-compatible store for higher throughput on one node.
taglines.dragonfly: Modern Redis-compatible store built for very high throughput.
taglines.mongodb: Document database for flexible, JSON-shaped data.
taglines.clickhouse: Column store for fast analytical queries over large event data.
taglines.meilisearch: Typo-tolerant full-text search with instant results over an HTTP API.
taglines.qdrant: Vector database for embeddings, semantic search and RAG retrieval.
taglines.typesense: Fast, typo-tolerant search engine with faceting and geo search.
taglines.memcached: Plain in-memory cache for sessions and query results. Nothing is kept on disk.

empty.title: No database matches "{{query}}"
empty.hint: Try an engine name such as Postgres or Redis, or clear the search to see every family.

list.title: Databases
list.emptyBody: Create a managed Postgres, MySQL or Redis database and connect an app to it. Credentials are injected for you.
list.errorBody: The databases list did not load. Check that the control plane is reachable, then try again.
list.description: Managed databases next to your apps, with backups and point in time restore.
list.pendingActionHint: Available once the database is created

detail.backupConfirmDescription: Starts a backup to the configured target right away.
detail.backupConfirmConsequence: The backup appears in the history below once it starts.

connection.forAppsHint: Apps on other nodes get this name and port. The tabs below show the address on the database's own node.
connection.title: Connection details
connection.description: How apps and tools reach this database.
connection.addressPrivateHint: Apps connected to this database receive the address and credentials automatically. Turn on public access to reach it from your machine.
connection.credentialsHint: Passwords are never shown here. Create a login or a temporary credential on the Access tab.
connection.passwordNever: Passwords are never shown here. Use the placeholder and create a login on the Access tab.
connection.unavailable: Connection details could not be loaded.

status.healthyHint: Running and passing every health check.
status.settingUpHint: Getting ready. This page updates on its own.
status.stoppedHint: Not running. Start it to accept connections.
status.attentionHint: Something failed. The logs show why.

conditions.title: Health checks
conditions.credentialsHelp: No secrets master key is configured, or this database's credentials failed to generate.

publicAccess.noPasswordWarning: This database has no password. Enabling public access lets anyone who can reach this host read and write the whole dataset with no authentication.
publicAccess.noPasswordOpen: This database has no password. This port is reachable from any network that can reach this host, granting full unauthenticated access.
publicAccess.openPort: This port is reachable from any network that can reach this host, not just your own machine. Make sure your firewall trusts that before relying on it in production.

custom.title: Not in the list? Run any database image
custom.description: Deploy it as a regular app with a volume for its data. You get deploys, logs, metrics and rollbacks, but not the managed features of the databases above: backups with restore checks, the data browser and the database commands in the CLI.

noBackups.title: Backups
noBackups.body: Backups are not available for {{engine}}: it keeps everything in memory and nothing on disk, so there is no data to back up.
noBackups.hint: A restart, upgrade or move starts it with an empty cache. Keep anything you cannot lose in a database that has backups.

links.title: Connected apps
links.description: Connect an app to inject this database connection string as an env var. It is encrypted at rest, never logged, and follows credential rotation the next time the app starts.
links.empty: No app is connected to this database yet.
links.noApps: There are no apps to connect yet.
links.toastConnectedBody: {{app}} gets the connection string as {{envVar}} on its next start.

banner.title: Databases
banner.description: Create a managed database beside your apps. Credentials are injected for you, backups run on a schedule, and you can restore to a point in time.
banner.whatFor: Pick an engine, accept the defaults, and your first database is running in under a minute. Already have one elsewhere? Connect it as an external database.

flow.title: Create a database
flow.description: Pick an engine and review the defaults. You can change everything later.
flow.name: Name
flow.versionHint: The recommended version is selected for you.
flow.sizeHint: Memory and CPU limits. Resize any time from the database page.
flow.backupsHint: Backups go to your first backup destination.
flow.noTarget: No backup destination yet, so backups stay off.
flow.secretsWarning: No secrets master key is configured, so this database is created but will not start until one is.

name.format: Use lowercase letters, numbers and dashes, starting with a letter or number.
name.taken: A database with this name already exists.

summary.empty: Choose an engine and a name to see a summary.

flow.createdPartial: Database "{{name}}" created, but size or backups could not be applied. Check its settings.
flow.dockerDown: Docker is not responding on this server. Databases cannot be created until it is back.

provision.title: Setting up your database

permission.title: Permission or capability denied
permission.hint: The container was denied a permission or capability. Check the host security profile and volume ownership.

out_of_memory.title: Out of memory
out_of_memory.hint: The database ran out of memory. Raise its memory limit.

port_in_use.title: Port already in use
port_in_use.hint: Another process already uses the port. Free it or pick another port.

bad_volume.title: Data volume corrupt or incompatible
bad_volume.hint: Restore a backup or start from a fresh volume.

bad_config.title: Configuration rejected
bad_config.hint: The database rejected its configuration. Review the settings you changed.

provision.confirmRemoveVolume: This deletes the old data volume for good. Continue?
provision.passwordNote: The password is never shown here. Open the database access page to manage credentials.
provision.leftoverVolume: A deleted database of this name left the volume {{name}} ({{size}}) behind.
provision.confirmDiscard: This deletes the saved settings of this database. Nothing was created. Continue?

backupSetup.title: Set up backups for {{name}}
backupSetup.saved: Backups scheduled for {{name}}. First backup started.

target.label: Where should backups go?
target.none: No backup destination is connected yet. Connect a bucket first, then come back here.

schedule.label: How often?
schedule.cronHint: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.

retention.label: How many backups to keep
retention.hint: Older backups beyond this count are deleted automatically.

run.progress: Running the first backup. This can take a few minutes for large databases.
run.done: First backup finished ({{size}}). Your schedule is active.

drill.none: Restore drill: not run yet. A drill proves a backup can really be restored.
drill.passed: Restore drill: the last drill passed.
drill.failed: Restore drill: the last drill failed. Check it before relying on these backups.

sizing.usageDescription: Last hour of real usage, so you can size limits from data.
sizing.stopped: The database is stopped, so there is no live usage to show. Start it to see memory and CPU.
sizing.noData: No usage samples yet. They appear within a minute of the database running.

headroom.tight: Tight: peak usage is close to the limit. Raise it before the database is killed.
headroom.ok: Reasonable headroom for the current load.
headroom.ample: Plenty of headroom. You could lower this and save memory.

impact.live: Applied to the running container right away, usually with no downtime. If it cannot be applied live, it waits for the next restart, which means about 5 seconds of downtime.
impact.stopped: The database is stopped, so nothing is interrupted. The limits take effect the next time it starts.
impact.none: Memory and CPU stay the same. Other settings apply on the next restart (about 5 seconds of downtime).

sizing.shrinkWarning: The new memory limit is below the peak seen in the last hour. The database may be killed for running out of memory.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.gapsSql: Connection counts and queries per second are not collected yet. To find slow statements, use
metrics.gapsMemory: Connection counts, operations per second and key evictions are not collected yet. Memory against its limit is the best early signal for this engine.

stopped.title: This database is stopped
stopped.body: There is nothing to chart while it is stopped. Start it and charts fill in within a minute or two.

provisioning.title: This database is still being created
provisioning.body: Metrics start once the database is running. Check progress on the overview page.
